etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Medieval Latin respectivus, from Latin respectus. Equivalent to respect +‎ -ive.

definitions.definition: Relating to particular persons or things, each to each; particular; own.

quote.citation: 2012 August 23, Alasdair Lamont, “Hearts 0-1 Liverpool”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Adam and Novikovas swapped long-range efforts, neither of which troubled the respective keepers.

quote.citation: 2020 April 22, “Network News: Staged return to work at Hitachi and CAF factories”, in Rail, page 9:
quote.text: Hitachi and CAF have begun a staged return to work at their respective Newton Aycliffe and Newport factories, having reduced output following the COVID-19 outbreak.

quote.citation: c. 1559-1570, Edwin Sandys, letter to Bernard Gilpin
quote.text: But if you looke upon the estate of the church of England with a respective eye , you cannot with a good conscience refuse this charge imposed upon you

definitions.definition: (obsolete) Looking toward; having reference to; relative, not absolute.

quote.citation: c. 1590–1591 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Two Gentlemen of Verona”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene iv], line 192:
quote.text: What should it be that he respects in her / But I can make respective in myself,

quote.citation: [1611?], Homer, “(please specify |book=I to XXIV)”, in Geo[rge] Chapman, transl., The Iliads of Homer Prince of Poets. […], London:  […]  Nathaniell Butter, →OCLC; republished as The Iliads of Homer, Prince of Poets, […], new edition, volume (please specify the book number), London: Charles Knight and Co., […], 1843, →OCLC:
quote.text: With a respective shame, rose, took us by the hands.The spelling has been modernized.

quote.citation: a. 1598, William Cecil, 1st Baron Burghley, instructions to his son Robert Cecil, when young
quote.text: With thy equals familiar, yet respective.
